newsitem.title: SPAIN: Folgado says prefers less peseta appreciation.
newsitem.headline: Folgado says prefers less peseta appreciation.

text.p: Spanish Budget Secretary Jose Folgado said on Monday he would prefer that the peseta had not appreciated so much against the mark.
"I would prefer that the exchange rate hadn't appreciated so much. But the market rules," Folgado told Reuters in an interview.
"We are near an equilibrium exchange rate," he added, and reiterated that the government would not rely on the exchange rate to solve any economic problems.
At 1235 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.12/14 per mark.

Earlier this month the peseta broke the key 84.00 per mark level. On January 16, the Bank of Spain cut its key money market rate by 25 basis points to 6.00 percent in an effort to tame the peseta's strength.
The Spanish currency bounced back above the 84.00 per mark level last week.
